topic: Claude plugins and skills for 2D animation pipelines
blind_spots: Very few raw first-person animator quotes; most evidence is Sonar-synthesized commentary rather than direct user voices.
No quantitative data on adoption, abandonment rates, latency, token cost, or render times for animation workflows.
No coverage of industry export formats (Lottie, MP4, image sequences), rigs, lip-sync, compositing, or audio sync.
No discussion of collaboration, version control, determinism, or team/multi-artist production workflows.
No accessibility considerations (e.g., prefers-reduced-motion) for generated web animations.
No analysis of IP/training-data provenance concerns for commercial animation production.
Several evidence timestamps are in the future (2026-05-27, 2026-06-17, 2026-06-20), suggesting the underlying source corpus may include hallucinated or fabricated dates that no panel model flagged.
contradictions: Anthropic/Brilliant framing of Claude Design as a 'step change' for prototyping interactive animations contrasts with widespread user reports of friction, choppy motion, and engineering complexity.
Claude pipelines are simultaneously described as 'rapid and flexible' at generating code and as failing to understand timing, staging, or design — a speed-vs-craft tension.
Specialized skills are presented as responses that address pain points, while users in the same evidence say those exact needs remain unmet.
The 'append mode is broken' Trustpilot complaint was treated by some panel models as evidence of animation-pipeline reliability, but the source provides no context tying it to 2D animation workflows.
